subject: Staged commit conversion + transient price shelter for BlueMarble renewal
messages:
From: Ari Gold <ari.gold@bluemarble.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <procurements@bluemarble.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + expanded committed capacity — request for price shelter and credits

Hi Aditya,

Hope you had a great long weekend. We’re starting procurement for our Redwood renewal and want to align on a path that supports a committed capacity increase and a short-term price shelter while we ramp to steady state. High-level: 12-month renewal, baseline commit + 30% additional committed capacity for Q3-Q4, and an expected burst profile for the first 8 weeks of the contract as we onboard a new product.

Ask: can Redwood offer a transient price shelter (3 months) at our current per-token pricing for baseline usage while we ramp, and a set of credits to offset any overages during that ramp? Procurement needs an initial terms note by next Friday (June 1) so we can issue a PO. Attached is our renewal request with usage projections.

Attachments: BlueMarble_Renewal_Request.pdf (summary + forecasts)

Appreciate a quick confirmation on whether this is something you can support, and if you have a recommended path (commit conversion, credits or invoice offsets).

Thanks,
Ari Gold
Head of ML, BlueMarble Systems
ari.gold@bluemarble.ai
+1 415-555-0132
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ari Gold <ari.gold@bluemarble.ai>, Samir Patel <procurements@bluemarble.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2028 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + expanded committed capacity — request for price shelter and credits

Ari — thanks for the clear note and the forecast. We can absolutely design a transitional structure that preserves your economics during ramp while protecting our ability to serve the increased baseline going forward. Proposed approach below (high level):

1) Staged commit conversion: baseline commit = current annualized commit; new commitment adds a 30% uplift for Q3–Q4. We propose a staged conversion where the additional capacity is recognized as a time-phased commit (50% effective for months 1–3, 75% months 4–6, 100% thereafter) with monthly true-ups.

2) Transient price shelter: 90-day price shelter on the baseline commit where we hold per-token pricing at current rates for baseline usage. The staged uplift will have a stepped-rate (to reflect risk) but we can cap the uplift to a maximum of 15% above current list for months 1–3 and step down to list thereafter.

3) Ramp credits: we’ll provide credits that can be applied as invoice offsets for the first two billing cycles that directly cover overages above the staged commit, capped at $50,000 total. Credits are intended to be a one-time ramp cushion and applied as invoice line-item credits (not refunds).

4) PO and invoicing: we are happy to align invoice timing to your procurement windows — we can invoice monthly with a 30-day payment term or offer a 3% prepay discount for upfront annual payment.

I’ve attached a draft with MSA redlines and the proposed term summary for your internal review. If you’re comfortable with this direction I’ll loop in revenue ops and legal (internal) for a quick sign-off and prepare a DocuSign packet.

Attachments: Draft_MSA_redlines_v2.docx (highlights on commit language + credit mechanics)

Next steps: Can you confirm (a) whether invoice offsets are acceptable to procurement, (b) target PO date (I hear June 1) and (c) whether BlueMarble will consider annual prepay?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Samir Patel <procurements@bluemarble.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + expanded committed capacity — request for price shelter and credits

Aditya — quick clarifications from procurement / finance: thanks for the thoughtful proposal. A couple of asks from our side before we circulate to legal and finance: 

- Can the ramp credits be applied as invoice offsets (yes/no)? We prefer offsets to speed reconciliation (avoids separate credit memos).
- Credit cap: $50k is fine in principle; can we see the math that led to that cap (sensitivity vs projected ramp)?
- Burst mechanics: what happens if we exceed staged commit in month 2 by 200% due to an integration spike — will you honor functional scaling or do we hit overage rates? We need an explicit overflow policy we can present.

PO target remains June 1. We would prefer monthly invoicing and applying credits as offsets rather than changing our payment cadence, but we will evaluate the 3% prepay discount with finance.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Samir
Head of Procurement, BlueMarble Systems
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + expanded committed capacity — pricing sign-off request

Marissa / Monica — forwarding BlueMarble’s request and my proposed structure. TL;DR: they want a 12-month renewal with +30% committed uplift, a 90-day price shelter on baseline, staged commit conversion, and two billing-cycle invoice-offset credits capped at $50k. Procurement prefers invoice offsets; PO target June 1.

Key commercial asks for approval: 
- Approve staged uplift schedule (50% / 75% / 100%) to avoid full immediate capacity reservation.
- Approve transient price shelter for baseline (90 days) and step-up cap of +15% on uplift months 1–3.
- Approve credit cap at $50k applied as invoice offsets (we may propose reducing cap if legal/finance prefer).
- Confirm that overflow policy will be: automatic elastic scaling; overage invoiced at list rate unless an emergency mitigation is requested (we can offer a 14-day write-off window for clearly-cataloged integration spikes, but that requires ops sign-off).

Estimated deal economics (back-of-envelope): annualized revenue ~ $420k if they fully convert. Credit cap exposure $50k (one-time).

Please reply with approved changes and any required constraints from finance/legal. If approved I’ll prepare the DocuSign with the updated MSA redlines and the deal summary for their procurement.

Full chain below for context.

—Aditya
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Ari Gold <ari.gold@bluemarble.ai>, Samir Patel <procurements@bluemarble.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + expanded committed capacity — request for price shelter and credits (final terms summary)

Ari / Samir — thanks for the quick clarifications and the patience. We had a short internal loop for pricing and finance. Here is the agreed commercial summary we can put into a 1–pager and the contract: 

1) Commit & ramp: 12-month renewal. Baseline commit = current annualized baseline. Additional committed uplift = 30% for Q3–Q4, applied as a staged conversion (50% effective months 1–3, 75% months 4–6, 100% thereafter) with monthly true-ups.

2) Transient price shelter: 90-day price shelter applies to baseline usage only; uplift usage billed per the staged rates (capped at +15% above current list for months 1–3).

3) Ramp credits & application: two billing-cycle credits applied as invoice offsets to cover overages above the staged commit, capped at $40,000 total (internal adjustment from $50k → $40k). Credits will appear as line-item offsets on invoices.

4) Overflow policy: automatic elastic scaling will keep services available. Any overages beyond staged commit billed at list; in cases of integration-caused spikes we will consider a one-time operational review within 14 days to approve mitigations — this is discretionary and requires an ops ticket.

5) Invoicing & PO: monthly invoicing with 30-day net terms. We also offer a 3% annual prepay option if BlueMarble elects to prepay for the 12 months.

Next steps: I’ll upload a 1‑pager to HubSpot and send the DocuSign packet once you confirm acceptance of these points. Per our internal review Marissa signed off on the adjusted credit cap and finance is OK with invoice-offset credits. 

DocuSign link (preview): https://docusign.net/ABC-1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Please reply with a brief confirmation and we’ll route the DocuSign to procurement for signature. If you need numbers behind the $40k cap, I can attach the sensitivity sheet — let me know.

Best regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
